subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. Nimbus vs. Atlas
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@omniva.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Competitive bake-off next steps (Redwood / Nimbus / Atlas)

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply if I missed anything.

Call highlights / pain:
- High token costs with current provider during peak hours (esp. long-form summaries & multi-turn chat).
- Variable latency on long-context requests ( > 8k tokens ) causing unhappy UX for clinicians.
- Need for private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) for regulated PHI workflows.

Decision criteria (what OmniVa prioritized):
1) Latency stability for 4–8k token sessions (p95 target < 600ms)
2) Cost per 1k tokens for expected volume (projected monthly ~4B tokens)
3) Security & audit controls (SOC2, KMS, VPC)
4) Ease of integration and rollout (API parity across hosted/dedicated/private)

Competitive notes from the call:
- Nimbus: strong native tooling, but we heard concerns about real-world latency at scale.
- Atlas: aggressive pricing on hosted endpoints but limited private deployment options today.
- Redwood: highlighted dedicated capacity + private deployment with predictable throughput; recommended model variants and quantization to reduce unit cost.

Next steps we agreed on:
- Redwood: deliver a short technical eval plan + scorecard for the bake-off (attached).
- OmniVa: provide two sample workloads (anonymized) and a short prioritization matrix for tests.
- Schedule: POC test window: Apr 26–30. We’ll run the same 3 scenarios across vendors.

Attachments: redwood_vs_competitors_scorecard.xlsx (scorecard + test matrix).

Proposed owners:
- Aditya (sales) — commercial & timeline
- Marissa (solutions) — POC design & metrics
- Rishi (tech) — infra & model config guidance
Available times for kickoff: Apr 22–23 between 9–12 PT — Laura, do any of these work?

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap: Competitive bake-off next steps (Redwood / Nimbus / Atlas)

Thanks Aditya — good capture. A few technical notes to add for OmniVa to consider for the POC:

Test scenarios (suggested):
- Scenario A (Interactive clinician chat): 2–4k token sessions, simulated concurrency 50–100 req/s. Measure p50/p95 latency and token cost.
- Scenario B (Long-form summarization): single request 8–12k tokens, measure memory/latency degradation and failure rate.
- Scenario C (Embeddings & rerank): high throughput smaller requests; measure tokens/sec and cost.

What we’ll supply for Redwood POC:
- Pre-configured model variants (quantized) and fixture scripts to reproduce load.
- Sample dashboard with latency/cost breakdown and KV cache hit rates.
- List of environment/security controls available in Private mode (SOC2 report stub, KMS integration guide).

Open questions for OmniVa (please confirm):
1) Can you share an anonymized example from Scenario B (long-form) we can use for accuracy/semantic quality checks?
2) Who is the procurement contact for contract timing/questions?

I’ll prepare the technical-eval-results.pdf and add suggested thresholds for pass/fail on each test.

—Marissa

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap: Competitive bake-off next steps (Redwood / Nimbus / Atlas)

Thanks, Aditya and Marissa — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can provide two anonymized long-form examples for Scenario B by end of day Apr 22. One will be ~9k tokens, the other ~11k tokens.
- Procurement contact is procurement@omniva.com (copied). They’ll need a short commercial summary and expected commit sizes after the POC.
- For the POC run: can Redwood and the other vendors each get the same k8s-based runner script? We want apples-to-apples (same load generator, same auth pattern).

Also — quick ask: can you include a short note (1 paragraph) on expected rollback behavior if a model variant causes regressions in quality during rollout? That’s one of our risk criteria.

We’re good to kick off Apr 26 — morning PT works for the kickoff (9:00 PT).

Best,
Laura Chen

Perfect — thanks Laura.

Quick answers:
- Yes, we’ll provide the same k8s-based runner script (we’ll upload to the shared Drive link).
- Rollback behavior (summary): Redwood’s rollout supports canary and automatic rollback triggers based on quality/regression alerts tied to the evaluation suite. If a model variant dips below the agreed threshold during a canary, traffic shifts automatically to the previous stable variant and we alert the on-call engineer. Full details (runbook) will be in the POC package.

Action items / owners:
- OmniVa: share anonymized samples for Scenario B by EOD Apr 22 -> Laura/Sanjay
- Redwood: upload runner script + detailed POC runbook by Apr 23 -> Marissa/Rishi
- Procurement: share any contract constraints (procurement@omniva.com)
- Kickoff: Apr 26, 09:00 PT (confirmed)

I’ll share calendar invite shortly. Looking forward to a productive bake-off.
